long_biography.plain_text:
In 1987, Robert S. “Bob” Berg and Steve Wemple acquired Sailormen, then an 11-restaurant Popeyes operator in Miami. The partners grew the business through relocations, new openings and acquisitions. By the turn of the century, Sailormen had completed eight further acquisitions and established operations across seven states. Berg led parent company Interfoods of America as chairman and chief executive.

The group narrowed its footprint by selling several state markets. Berg subsequently left day-to-day leadership, and the company continued under new executives before filing for Chapter 11 protection in 2026. The court-supervised process sought a sale of substantially all its assets, leaving the present economic relationship between Berg and the restaurant platform unclear.
long_biography.html:
In 1987, Robert S. “Bob” Berg and Steve Wemple acquired Sailormen, then an 11-restaurant Popeyes operator in Miami. The partners grew the business through relocations, new openings and acquisitions. By the turn of the century, Sailormen had completed eight further acquisitions and established operations across seven states. Berg led parent company Interfoods of America as chairman and chief executive.

The group narrowed its footprint by selling several state markets. Berg subsequently left day-to-day leadership, and the company continued under new executives before filing for Chapter 11 protection in 2026. The court-supervised process sought a sale of substantially all its assets, leaving the present economic relationship between Berg and the restaurant platform unclear.
